title: Converge ext4 Tier 1 lifecycle ownership

steps.notes: Completed at a16958f2. Writeback leases and read targets are retained at admission by OwnedFileIoRequest; every initial/resume planning and queue failure reaches its one terminalizer. steps.title: Add MutationHandle and owned cross-yield tokens
steps.notes: Completed: private MutationHandle now owns prepared journal records, optional JournalExtentToken, data/commit request IDs, phase-local error state, and checkpoint retry state. JournalFsyncSource is a compatibility re-export but its callback orchestration moved to mutation_lifecycle.rs; a data failure consumes the handle and releases its ring extent exactly once. This bounded slice retains the existing immutable after-images inside PreparedJournalTransaction but does not yet add explicit frozen-read/allocator-claim tokens, AbortDraining, CommitUnknown/RecoveryOnly, or real FUA/flush durability. Verified cargo test -p tx-ext4 --test mutation_lifecycle, cargo test -p tx-ext4 --test journal_prepared_transaction, cargo test -p tx-ext4 --lib --no-default-features, cargo -q xtask unit, scoped rustfmt/diff checks. cargo xtask lint arch ran: the touched ext4 journal length finding was eliminated, but the repository still has 90 unrelated pre-existing architecture lint findings.

steps.title: Close abort drain, commit uncertainty, and checkpoint retry
steps.notes: Completed: MutationHandle now records AbortRequested -> AbortDraining -> RolledBack for known pre-commit data or commit failure, releasing its JournalExtentToken once the aggregate graph completion reports terminal failure. The explicit commit_unknown request-ID path retains the handle and ring extent, records the source error, and gates new writeback/fsync planning with RecoveryOnly/EIO. Checkpoint failure records a source error but retains CommittedNeedsSettlement and its extent for retry; a later successful checkpoint is still the sole release route. This source-local gate precedes Task 13 errseq/open-file cursor and mounted-instance publication; Task 7 still must prove real FUA/flush ordering. Verified lifecycle, prepared-transaction, ext4 library, workspace unit, scoped rustfmt, and diff checks.

steps.title: Implement real FUA and flush durability
steps.notes: Completed: BlockDeviceOps exposes immutable FUA/flush capabilities plus write options; BlockDeviceDispatchAdapter transfers BlockFlags::FUA to a capable device and rejects unsupported FUA rather than silently dropping it. RV64 virtio PCI/MMIO truthfully advertise flush=true and fua=false because the present virtio driver exposes flush but no FUA write API. JournalTransactionPlan therefore emits ordered explicit flush fences after the journal body and commit, plus after the clean checkpoint write, rather than attaching an unsupported FUA flag. Verified dispatch_adapter_passes_fua_to_capable_device, default_device_rejects_fua_instead_of_ignoring_it, journal_transaction_plan (3), mutation_lifecycle (4), cargo check -p tx-drivers, cargo -q xtask unit (639 tx-shims tests), scoped rustfmt, and git diff --check. This does not admit a production RW path, runtime device-capability selection, tail/cache settlement, replay, or QEMU durability evidence; Task 8 remains next.

steps.title: Gate replay on recovery state and refresh caches
steps.notes: Completed: recovery admission exposes Superblock::needs_recovery and recover_if_required; a clean ext4 superblock skips stale JBD2 replay, while recovery-required runs replay plus durable journal clean. JBD2 superblock CRC32C has valid and invalid witnesses; unsupported descriptor/commit checksum layouts fail closed. BlockImage::barrier is mandatory and the production bridge forwards it to the registered block device. RW admission persists recovery-required before a journalled mutation. A weak mount settlement observer invalidates pager image, extent mapping, lookup, directory, inode metadata, and bridge block caches after durable checkpoint; JournalExtentToken remains retained until that settlement returns, then tail reclaim releases it. Verified jbd2_recovery (9), pager_mock (17), tx-ext4 library (35), mutation_lifecycle (5), tx-fs bridge (6), scoped rustfmt, and git diff --check. This is not product recovery acceptance: Task 9 revoke/deferred-free, complete mutation vertical slices, mount settlement, production cutover, QEMU crash, e2fsck, and xfstests evidence remain pending.

steps.title: Add revoke records and deferred-free ownership
steps.notes: Completed: immutable Ext4MutationPlan values canonicalize paired RevokeRecord and DeferredFreeClaim entries; JBD2 reserves and stages an optional revoke page between metadata and commit, and its durable graph orders that page before commit. MutationHandle owns the deferred-free claims from admission through cache observer settlement and JournalExtentToken tail reclaim, so test-only reuse remains EBUSY until tail reclaim. Replay recognizes the optional revoke page, validates its sequence, includes it in cursor accounting, and suppresses matching same-transaction stale after-images. Verified jbd2_transaction_image (2), jbd2_recovery (10), journal_transaction_plan (4), mutation_lifecycle (6), cargo -q xtask unit (639 + 114 + 35 + 166), scoped rustfmt, and git diff --check. steps.title: Migrate buffered data, bounded extents, and truncate
steps.notes: In progress: truncate now has production mutation admission for metadata-only size changes and the first bounded reclaim shape. Ext4Pager::plan_truncate_size preserves unknown inode bytes, refreshes metadata_csum, and for inline extent-leaf files can release complete tail blocks in one block group by updating the inode extent root and block count, clearing the block bitmap, incrementing group/superblock free counters, and emitting paired JBD2 revoke plus deferred-free claims. FsPageBacking::truncate on mutation-journal mounts routes both metadata-only and bounded tail-free plans through JournalMutationRuntime::begin_mutation without direct home writes; read-only mounts still return EROFS and mounts without a metadata mutation runtime still return EOPNOTSUPP. PageBacked now has a retained multi-page PageDataLease constructor that projects multi-page payload as neutral IoDataSource::Direct vecs while preserving the existing single-page PageCache projection, and FileFsyncFrontier can derive stable contiguous range/generation batches from a captured frontier. The fsync frontier consumes contiguous same-generation batches in actual PageBacked writeback admission: one L4 PageIoRange retains one multi-page OwnedFileIoRequest, exposes a Direct vec source to the backend, and settles every PageSlot in the completion range before releasing the owner row. The ext4 L5 writeback mutation planner has direct tests proving a mutation-runtime-bound provider accepts already-mapped multi-page Direct requests, rejects malformed Direct vec shapes, and the journal bridge splits a multi-page Direct source into one ordered-data node per page before the durability fence. New in the 2026-08-01 public writeback slice: FsPageBacking::flush_page on mutation-journal mounts no longer calls require_mutation_owner plus the legacy direct pager write; it snapshots the dirty frame, asks Ext4Pager::plan_write_page for the immutable writeback mutation, and admits it through JournalMutationRuntime::begin_mutation. Tests now prove both mapped public flush and bounded single-page hole growth admit a transaction frontier without writing the home image; read-only and no-runtime mounts remain fail-closed. steps.title: Add MountSettlementOp, errseq, and syscall routing
steps.notes: In progress: the mount-side scaffold has default FsOps::shutdown plus FsOps::settle_file/settle_mount hooks, a MountRuntimeCell-backed MountSettlementOp that owns a MountPayloadPin while active, records detach shutdown errors through ErrorSeq, and drives successful detach to Detached or failure to RecoveryOnly. SettlementScope::File now carries the FsObjectId plus a captured FileFsyncFrontier generation frontier; sys_fsync snapshots that PageBacked frontier once, drives FileFsyncOp from the same value, and passes it through MountSettlementOp into the backend settle_file hook. JournalMutationRuntime now exposes snapshot_transaction_frontier(), backed by the active MutationHandle transaction sequence, and FsOps::snapshot_mount_transaction_frontier() can route mount-wide sync/syncfs settlement to that JBD2 frontier. Metadata-only mutations without a data graph enter Prepared directly so their commit graph can be driven by fsync/sync settlement. Ext4 overrides settle_file and settle_mount to settle mount-local pager/mapping/lookup/directory/inode caches without releasing the backend-held mount pin; detach shutdown still owns that release. Syscall routing covers sync, syncfs, fsync, fdatasync, and namespace-backed umount2: sync snapshots visible mount payload pins and preserves the Linux success return contract; syncfs observes mount errors through the calling open-file description and drives mount-scope settlement; fsync/fdatasync observe payload errors through the calling open-file description and drive file-scope settlement after FileFsyncOp with the captured generation frontier; normal namespace umount checks active payload users before quiesce and topology withdrawal; MNT_FORCE returns EOPNOTSUPP; MNT_DETACH withdraws topology and leaves active payload users in DetachedPending. OpenFile stores mount/payload errseq cursors shared by dup/forked file descriptions and samples the current mount sequence when opened through the walker, bootstrap create, or open_by_handle_at. Lazy detach has a background mount-settlement queue that registers a retained MountSettlementOp when the final payload user releases and keeps retryable detach operations queued across EAGAIN. The legacy namespace-less umount branch remains topology-only because the global helper does not return the removed mount identity. Verified cargo test -p tx-subsystems --lib settlement_lifecycle_tests -- --test-threads=1 (11), cargo test -p tx-subsystems --lib page_backed -- --test-threads=1 (154), cargo test -p tx-shims --lib fd_ops_wave2 -- --test-threads=1 (52), cargo test -p tx-ext4 --lib --no-default-features (39), cargo test -p tx-ext4 --test mutation_lifecycle -- --test-threads=1 (7), cargo -q xtask unit (646 + 114 + 39 + 166), and scoped rustfmt. steps.title: Add one cargo xtask ext4 tier1 runner
steps.notes: RunWorkspace now exists and owns temporary directories, child-process cleanup, authority hashing, and failure receipts for the public `cargo xtask ext4 tier1` entry. The command dispatch, dry-run authority resolution, and acceptance-receipt draft shape are in place, and the pinned shell scenario now uses an explicit `#!/bin/busybox sh` execute-from-scratch script shape backed by tx-scripts shebang argv tests. New in the 2026-08-02 G0/preflight slice: the live runner now rejects placeholder xfstests and crash-cut authority statuses before full-build/QEMU, so it cannot mint a false G0-G7 passed receipt from declared-but-not-acceptance-ready manifests. New in the source-lock slice: `XfstestsSelection` requires `source_lock`, dry-run prints the pinned xfstests path/revision/check sha256, `ensure_xfstests_root` checks out the manifest revision instead of a hard-coded constant, and the runner verifies the actual xfstests checkout revision plus `check` sha256 before running selected cases. New in the crash-cut fail-closed slice: `run_crash_cut_campaign` refuses to synthesize `completed=1000` from the crash catalog until deterministic crash/replay execution is wired, and `Tier1AcceptanceReceipt::from_live` derives G1-G7 from crash/e2fsck/xfstests evidence instead of unconditionally marking them passed. New in the xfstests parser slice: zero exit from `./check` is no longer sufficient; the runner requires a `Passed all N tests` summary matching the selected case count and fails closed on not-run/failure/missing-summary output. New in the e2fsck coverage-gate slice: `from_live` now keeps G1-G7 blocked unless e2fsck evidence includes TEST/SCRATCH/WORKLOAD plus at least one immutable image per completed crash cut, every e2fsck result has exit code 0 and a nonzero 64-hex sha256, and the xfstests passed count matches the authority-selected case count. New in the SCRATCH matrix slice: the live runner's guest operation matrix now attaches `scratch.img` through `--extra-rv64-ext4` instead of accidentally running against `workload.img`; a focused xtask test rejects shell args containing `test.img` or `workload.img` for that matrix. New in the three-drive foundation slice: RV64 platform info exposes `virtio0..2`, kernel block init registers successful slots as `vda/vdb/vdc` while moving fallback `ltpdev` to `DevT(254,255)`, and qemu/shell-test accept repeated `--extra-rv64-ext4` values rendered as `txblk0..2` on `virtio-mmio-bus.0..2`. New in the role-scenario slice: `run_live_tier1` passes TEST/SCRATCH/WORKLOAD images in stable device order, the shell scenario verifies TEST, mounts WORKLOAD read-only and observes EROFS on write, then mounts SCRATCH read-write for all eight operation groups. Dynamic ext4 `sys_mount` now uses the discovered-journal RW path plus `Ext4FileIoRuntimeBinder`, matching boot `/musl` instead of the old planner-only `mount_ext4_read_write(image)` path. New in the G0 lint sequence slice: dry-run now lists `run G0 ext4 ownership and durability lints` as the first product action, and live Tier 1 runs `ext4-lifecycle-ownership`, `ext4-no-direct-home-write`, and `ext4-durability-flags` before build/QEMU once authority manifests are acceptance-ready. New in the crash-campaign e2fsck evidence-boundary slice: `run_crash_cut_campaign` now returns typed `CrashCutCampaignEvidence`, its constructor rejects completed crash counts without matching immutable e2fsck image records, and the live receipt path appends those crash-image records to TEST/SCRATCH/WORKLOAD e2fsck results before computing failures. New in the crash-campaign-plan slice: an acceptance-ready crash catalog must declare a `campaign` object with repo-relative workload/replay scripts, `kill_policy=deterministic-phase-marker-v1`, and `e2fsck_mode=immutable-copy`; dry-run prints the campaign plan when present, so changing only `status` cannot bypass missing execution inputs. New in the crash-campaign-manifest slice: failed run workspaces now preserve generated artifacts, and a campaign-backed crash catalog writes `crash-campaign-plan.json` with schema `tx.ext4.crash_cut_execution_manifest.v1`, all 1000 deterministic cut IDs, stable family assignment, workload/replay scripts, kill policy, e2fsck mode, and per-cut immutable image names before the executor fails closed. New in the crash-campaign-inputs slice: the placeholder crash catalog now names real workload/replay scripts while remaining non-promotable, `CrashCutCatalog::load_with_root` verifies those scripts exist and records their sha256, dry-run prints the hashes, and the generated execution manifest carries the same hashes per run. New in the crash-outcome boundary slice: `CrashCutOutcome` and `CrashCutCampaignEvidence::from_outcomes()` require matching per-cut outcome rows with clean e2fsck and replay exits before crash images can become receipt evidence. New in the crash-outcome-manifest consumption slice: after writing `crash-campaign-plan.json`, `run_crash_cut_campaign` now consumes a same-workspace `crash-cut-outcomes.json` through `CrashCutCampaignEvidence::from_outcome_manifest()` when present, records it as a run artifact, and otherwise still fails closed while naming the expected outcome path. This wires real executor output into the same receipt aggregation boundary instead of leaving the parser unused. New in the phase-marker contract slice: campaign-backed crash catalogs now require every D0-D12 family to carry a unique `phase_marker` for `deterministic-phase-marker-v1`, and `crash-campaign-plan.json` writes those markers into both the family table and every expanded cut row. This gives the future QEMU killer a stable manifest-owned serial marker contract instead of requiring it to infer cut points from labels. steps.title: Close G0-G7 with fresh product evidence
steps.notes: Promote only from the immutable receipt covering all 1000 deterministic crash cuts, fresh SCRATCH operation matrix, pinned xfstests, and post-run e2fsck. Receipt gates are now evidence-derived and require e2fsck coverage for TEST/SCRATCH/WORKLOAD plus at least every completed crash cut; missing crash/e2fsck/xfstests proof, dirty e2fsck exits, placeholder image hashes, or xfstests count mismatches leave G1-G7 blocked instead of passed. Current fresh normal-lifecycle role probe `target/ext4/probe/tier1-role-*-destroy-free-close-20260802062938.img` passes the full 8-group QEMU TEST/SCRATCH/WORKLOAD scenario, and TEST/SCRATCH/WORKLOAD all pass offline `e2fsck -fn` exit 0. The public runner now includes the G0 ext4 ownership/direct-write/durability lint stage before build/QEMU in its live product sequence, and its crash campaign boundary now requires completed crash cuts to carry matching immutable e2fsck image records before receipt aggregation. An acceptance-ready crash catalog must also declare executable workload/replay/kill/e2fsck campaign inputs, and campaign-backed failure paths preserve a generated `tx.ext4.crash_cut_execution_manifest.v1` artifact with all 1000 cut IDs and script hashes, so current placeholder authorities cannot be promoted by status-only edits. Per-cut crash outcomes must also prove clean e2fsck and replay before they aggregate into receipt image evidence. The public runner now consumes a same-workspace `crash-cut-outcomes.json` after writing the deterministic campaign manifest, but only clean parsed outcomes can aggregate and the receipt gate still requires `completed == required == 1000`. risks: A direct pager call can create a second durability domain unless G0 rejects every production callsite.
A committed transaction with checkpoint failure requires retained authority and retry; treating it as rollback corrupts the live view.
FUA metadata without device capability enforcement can make fsync appear durable while the medium is not ordered.
Lazy detach can withdraw topology while DMA or settlement remains live; the MountPayload pin must outlive topology removal.
Host contract tests and reused serial logs can be mistaken for product evidence without fresh QEMU, immutable image, e2fsck, and xfstests receipts.
blockers: 2026-08-02 close/dup3 visibility flush unblocked the previous `--group data,execute-from-scratch` QEMU failure, and a fresh wider QEMU run with `--group data,setattr,namespace,orphan,execute-from-scratch` passed 5 groups with 0 failures; do not promote Tier 1 until the remaining production cutover, FUA/recovery, live runner, crash-cut, e2fsck, xfstests, and immutable receipt gates close.

Task 14 G0 lints now pass in the current checkout and the former `namespace.rs`/`pager.rs` direct-home-write allowlist has been retired, but production cutover still lacks FUA/recovery product gates and the final live Tier 1 acceptance evidence.
Current block adapter ignores FUA flags and replay does not yet use the ext4 recovery-required gate on every production path.

The public `cargo xtask ext4 tier1` command exists, verifies the manifest-pinned xfstests source lock, parses xfstests output fail-closed, refuses to synthesize crash-cut completion or unconditional passed gates, and now routes per-cut fault jobs through the repository executor with bound request/result/log/image evidence. Live execution still correctly fails closed while xfstests/crash authorities remain placeholder statuses; no full 1000-cut run, pinned xfstests execution, or immutable G0-G7 receipt has been produced.
